items.title: Review and add Afrikaans layer-template translations
items.description: ## The problem The reference site's earthquake, GDACS and country cards and lists include English words around provider-supplied values. The keyed layer-template mechanism in #369 lets a host translate those words, but the Afrikaans translations need a fluent review before they can ship. ## What is wanted Add reviewed Afrikaans translations for the reference site's keyed layer templates. Keep provider-supplied names and values as published, preserve every field and formatter in each translated template, and load the translations only when Afrikaans is chosen. ## Accessibility and data use Keep the existing keyboard and screen-reader behaviour, including slider value text. This should make no new network requests beyond loading the selected language's own bundle. ## Tasks - [ ] Start with failing tests for the translated card and list wrappers, field placeholders and provider-supplied values. - [ ] Add the host's Afrikaans layer-template translations and load them with the Afrikaans catalogue. - [ ] Have someone fluent in Afrikaans review every new translation before it ships, and name the reviewer in the pull request. - [ ] Run the relevant layer, language, accessibility and visual checks; update `docs/guides/translate-the-sdk.md` and `docs/guides/performance.md` if their descriptions change. Part of #316; follows #268.

items.title: graphty-element: canvas background does not follow light and dark theme
items.description: ## Problem The graph background defaults to a fixed `whitesmoke` whatever the page's colour scheme. In a dark UI (the graphty app's default, or any consumer's dark mode) the canvas is a bright rectangle. A consumer can set `element.background` by hand, but must detect the scheme and re-set it on every change -- work every consumer repeats. ## Where - `graphty-element/src/config/GraphStyle.ts:88` -- `background` defaults to `{ backgroundType: "color", color: "whitesmoke" }`. - `graphty-element/src/Graph.ts:726-727` -- the colour is applied as-is. - No `prefers-color-scheme` handling anywhere in `graphty-element/src`. ## Expected The element offers a theme-aware background: for example `background: "auto"` (or a light/dark pair) that follows `prefers-color-scheme` or a `color-scheme` / theme attribute on the element, with default label and edge colours that stay legible on both. ## Acceptance - [ ] A documented way to get light and dark backgrounds without consumer code watching the scheme. - [ ] Switching the scheme repaints without reloading data. - [ ] Test: emulate dark scheme and read the applied clear colour. - [ ] The graphty app uses it and sets no background itself.

items.title: The TPO chart type has no block colour, profile period or split display settings
items.description: ### Problem The TPO chart type's settings live in `ChartTypeParams` (`src/model/chart_type.rs:869-899`) and its series settings (`src/ui/dialogs/series_settings/tabs/symbol.rs:738-807`): period, initial balance, rows, value area, sessions and visibility switches. Several settings of a TPO profile are missing: - Colours: blocks are always coloured by period from a fixed palette, and blocks outside the value area are always dimmed by a fixed 0.45 blend towards the background (`src/chart/rendering/candles/tpo.rs:740`). There is no switch between coloured and single colour blocks, no choice of the colours a profile's blocks run through, and no opacity for blocks outside the value area. - Profile period: `to_tpo_profiles` builds one profile per trading session, or per calendar day without trading hours (`src/model/tpo.rs:388-429`). Longer profiles exist only as composites merged by hand from the context menu, one range at a time. - Split display: `TPODisplayMode` offers letters, blocks or both (`src/model/tpo.rs:174-181`), and every mode collapses each period's letters into one profile. No display leaves each period's blocks in a column of their own. ### Expected The TPO chart type offers, with the current look as defaults: - coloured blocks on or off, off drawing every block in one colour; the colours the blocks of a profile run through; the opacity of blocks outside the value area; - a profile period: session, the default, or a week or a month, each profile then covering every session that opens within that period, with its letters, value area and statistics computed over them; - a split display in which each period's blocks stay in their own column at the period's position. ### Done when - [ ] Each colour setting changes the painted blocks of a multi-period profile in both themes, and the defaults paint as today; a rendering test asserts the block colours. - [ ] With a weekly period, five daily sessions draw one profile whose point of control and value area equal those of a composite over the same sessions; a test builds weekly and monthly profiles. - [ ] With the split display a session of four periods draws four columns, each holding exactly the rows its period touched, and the value area, point of control and statistics are unchanged. - [ ] Ok, Cancel, undo and saved layouts keep each value, and layouts saved without the settings load the current look.

items.title: Anchored volume profiles cannot size rows in ticks or start at earnings, dividends or splits
items.description: ### Problem The anchored volume profile studies offer fewer row and anchor choices than the other profile studies: - Row size: the session and periodic studies offer "Height in ticks", which makes rows a whole number of the instrument's ticks. Vol Profile Anchored and Vol Profile Auto Anchored offer only Row count and a height in price units, because the input is added only for the session and periodic kinds (`src/studies/builtin/volume_profile.rs:358-366`); `set_input("row_ticks", 4)` on either returns `unknown study input "row_ticks"`. A user who wants rows of 4 ticks has to work out the price height by hand, and that height does not follow the instrument when the symbol changes. - Anchor: the Anchor input of Vol Profile Auto Anchored offers the interval default, the highest high, lowest low or highest volume in a lookback, and calendar periods (`ANCHORS`, `src/studies/builtin/volume_profile.rs:222-234`). It cannot start the profile at the latest earnings report, dividend or split, although the anchored VWAP study already anchors on them through the events the chart holds (`VwapAnchor::{Earnings, Dividends, Splits}` and `Indicator::set_time_scale_events`, `src/studies/builtin/vwap.rs:542-556`). ### Expected - The anchored and auto anchored studies offer the same row layout as the session and periodic studies: a row count, a row height in ticks of the chart instrument, or a height in price units. - Anchor also offers Earnings, Dividends and Splits. Each starts the profile at the first bar at or after the latest event of that kind supplied through `Chart::set_time_scale_events`. Without such an event no profile is drawn, and a new event moves the profile. ### Done when - [ ] "Height in ticks" is listed for Vol Profile Anchored and Vol Profile Auto Anchored. With a 0.25 tick and 4 ticks, their profiles have rows 1.0 high; the cases of `session_rows_follow_whole_ticks_of_the_instrument` are extended to both studies. - [ ] Vol Profile Auto Anchored lists Earnings, Dividends and Splits after the existing choices, so saved choice indices keep their meaning. - [ ] With dividend events on two dates, the profile starts at the bar of the later one, and adding a later event moves it. - [ ] Tests cover both and fail on the current code.

items.title: feat(fuzz): expose sequence execution in sdkt fuzz campaign
items.description: ## Context Sequence execution is the part of the fuzz engine that exercises state carry between invocations — the class of bug that only appears when a second call observes what the first one wrote. The engine implements it, the artifact format records it, and replay already handles it, but it is unreachable from the CLI that release-assurance users actually run. ## Problem `CampaignInput` exposes `sequence_length` and `sequence_every` as public fields (`crates/sdkt-fuzz/src/campaign.rs:77-79`), and the campaign runner already branches on them (`campaign.rs:213-215`) and already executes multi-step sequences through `execute_sequence_auth` with per-step auth (`campaign.rs:295`, `campaign.rs:335`). The generated sequence is built from `sequence_length` (`campaign.rs:227`). `CampaignConfig` already records both settings (`artifact.rs:180-183`), and replay already handles multi-step artifacts (`replay.rs:203-204`). The CLI never sets them. `crates/sdkt-cli/src/commands/fuzz.rs` contains no reference to either field, and `sdkt fuzz campaign --help` exposes no flag for them. Because `sequence_every` defaults to `0` (`campaign.rs:100`), `is_sequence` is always false on the CLI path, so every campaign run through `sdkt fuzz campaign` is single-step only. The repository documents this gap itself: `docs/reference/fuzz-real-contract-evidence.md:460` states "CLI v2.7.0 lacks `--sequence`; sequence evidence uses the public library API (path-dependency probe, zero source modification)." There is also no regression coverage for the campaign sequence path. `git grep -n "sequence_every"` across the repository returns only source occurrences plus one test that sets it to `0` to disable sequencing (`crates/sdkt-fuzz/tests/oracle_minimizer_campaign.rs:500`). No test runs a campaign with `sequence_every > 0`. Consequence: the state-carry path is dead code for CLI users, and the library-level sequence evidence cannot be reproduced with the shipped binary. ## Contributor Task Expose the existing sequence capability on the CLI and cover it with tests: 1. Add `--sequence-length ` and `--sequence-every ` to `sdkt fuzz campaign`, mapped onto the existing `CampaignInput` fields. 2. Validate the pair before running: supplying only one of the two flags is a usage error, and values below the engine's minimum (`sequence_length >= 2`, `sequence_every >= 1`) are rejected with an actionable message. 3. Keep the default behaviour identical to today when neither flag is given. 4. Surface seq

items.title: Record a Claude seat's current Remote Control session on the node read
items.description: ## What I am trying to do A small status page for the operator lists a rig's seats, and clicking a Claude seat should open that seat's Remote Control conversation in the Claude app (`https://claude.ai/code/session_ `). The page reads OpenRig's node projection and nothing else. It should never build the link from a guess or read a seat's transcript. ## What stops it - Claude Code documents one local source for the id: `CLAUDE_CODE_BRIDGE_SESSION_ID`, set in the session's own Bash tool and hook subprocesses while Remote Control is connected, and removed when it disconnects (Claude Code docs, environment variables; v2.1.199 and later). Status-line and hook inputs carry no such field, and no CLI command returns it. - A reconnect after a connection failure can replace the server session if compaction or a conversation switch happened meanwhile, so a saved link can become stale ([Claude Code docs, what connected devices see](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/remote-control#what-connected-devices-see)). - On OpenRig 0.7.18 (3bf87c62), the node read (`rig ps --nodes --json`) has no field for it. The daemon notices `--remote-control` only while tracing process lineage. Outside that read, the id shows in the session's own terminal status panel (not something a page should parse) and in the transcript, whose format Claude Code calls internal. OpenRig already runs its own hook relay inside managed Claude seats (`activity-relay.cjs`, which forwards the session identity on every SessionStart, see #1077), which is exactly where the variable is documented to exist. ## Proposed direction Could the existing Claude hook bridge record the current value of `CLAUDE_CODE_BRIDGE_SESSION_ID` (or its absence) on the hook events it already receives, and expose it on the node read as an optional field, for example `remoteControl: { sessionId, observedAt } | null`? - Present only while the seat's latest hook saw the variable; null when it was absent, for Codex seats, or before any hook ran. - The session id only, never a token or account detail. A consumer can build the documented `claude.ai/code` link from it. - No new watcher or transcript read; it rides on the hook events OpenRig already handles. ## Behavior to verify - A seat with Remote Control connected shows the id after its next hook event, and it matches the link in the Claude app. - When the server session is replaced (such as a reconnect after a failure across compaction or a conversation switch), the field updates on the nex

items.title: Let a person's own page answer what needs them (team-operations.v1 needs-me.answer), without a grant service
items.description: ## What I am trying to do A small page on the operator's own devices shows what needs them across their rigs, from `GET /api/attention?view= `, and lets them answer an ask or a park from that page. The read works today. I would like the answer to go through the same native path Steering and `rig_question_answer` use, so the asker's work continues exactly once and the audit names the route. ## What stops it On OpenRig 0.7.18 (3bf87c62): - `GET /api/team-operations/capabilities` reports `needs-me.read: supported`, `needs-me.answer: not-supported`, `needs-me.follow: not-supported`. - `rig_question_list` and `rig_question_answer` are offered only to an external grant-service connection whose grant names a registered person. A file grant from `rig mcp token add` has no person option, and an owner grant or stdio server doesn't get these two tools either (`offered()` in `dist/mcp-server.js`; `docs/reference/hosted-members.md`, "A person answering the team's questions through their assistant"). So a single-operator install has to run its own `openrig.grant/v1` service just to let the person answer their own questions from a page, or copy Steering's write route in its own code. Related, not the same: #3470 (an operator cockpit pane showing what waits on them) is about where the person sees these; this is about answering them from their own page. ## Proposed direction Either of these would do; which shape do you prefer? 1. **A person on a file grant:** `rig mcp token add --seat --person ` (the entity registered with `rig gateway human add`). With it, that grant gets `rig_question_list` and `rig_question_answer`, acting for that person exactly as the grant-service form does today. Without `--person`, nothing changes. 2. **needs-me.answer in team-operations.v1:** an HTTP answer write next to the read, naming the request, its `revision` (as `expectedRevision`) and the choices or words, with the same outcomes `rig_question_answer` returns (`answered`, `recorded`, `already-recorded`, `question_changed`, `not_waiting_on_person`, `person_not_registered`). The capability flips to `supported`. Both keep today's rules: never another person's question, never a team-internal row, never a decision of the caller's own; a stale revision is refused rather than overwriting a newer answer. ## Behavior to verify - The person's grant lists and answers only their own asks and parks; another person's question and a team-internal row are refused. - An answer with a stale revision returns

items.title: Support an optional bounded wait on the MCP queue-show tool
items.description: ## What I am trying to do An assistant delegates a task to an OpenRig seat, keeps its queue item ID, and reads the seat's answer from that same item. I would like one read call to wait briefly for completion, rather than require another user turn or repeated immediate reads. ## What stops it On OpenRig 0.7.18, the MCP tool schemas expose: - rig_queue_show: qitemId and optional host; it returns the current item and transitions immediately. - rig_chatroom_watch: rigName, topic, sender and limit; it returns current history and explicitly does not wait. I verified this with tools/list on an authenticated native HTTP server. A seat-only credential can already read its task through queue-show. Chatroom access has a different scope and still would not provide a blocking answer wait. rig_send's waitForIdleSeconds waits before sending to a pane, rather than for a delegated task's answer. ## Proposed direction Could the existing rig_queue_show tool support an optional bounded wait for the named item's completion, keeping its current immediate behavior when omitted? The call would return immediately if the result is already available. Otherwise it would wait up to the requested bound, then return either the current native task record or an explicit pending/timeout indication. It should preserve the existing authorization, item/transition projection and handoff successor information. A handoff or denied/canceled task must remain distinguishable from an answered task; waiting must not invent an answer or create a second task. The intended bound is roughly a minute, subject to the project's preferred API and limits. Prefer the daemon's existing event mechanism if suitable. No new chatroom, rig-wide grant, wrapper service or background watcher is proposed. ## Behavior to verify - A result present before the call returns immediately; a result arriving during the wait returns promptly. - No result produces a bounded pending outcome; unrelated progress or another task cannot satisfy completion. - Current read scope and revoked/out-of-scope refusals remain intact; cancellation releases the waiter. - The native HTTP transport supports the bounded call, and a disconnected caller can read the same task again without creating work twice. - Calls without the option retain today's behavior. I have not changed the installed daemon or built this feature. I am opening the direction question first, as CONTRIBUTING.md requests. Which completion predicate and API shape would you prefer?

items.title: feat: specify and verify resumable incremental transcript capture across Codex rollouts
items.description: ## Problem Cortex reads Codex rollouts and deduplicates profile updates by session. Those inspected paths do not establish a replayable append contract across continuation files, late delivery, transcript rewrites and lost acknowledgements. This is a bounded investigation finding, not proof that every capture path lacks a cursor. ## Proposed solution Audit all capture producers first. Reuse any existing cursor/idempotency mechanism; otherwise define durable progress, source identity, prefix rewrite detection and delivery identity. ## Acceptance evidence - [ ] One logical session spans two rollout files; a late event from the first file cannot drop the second file. - [ ] Repeat delivery and simulate acceptance followed by acknowledgement loss; the final retained conversation has no missing or duplicated turns. - [ ] Modify an earlier turn and expose replacement/reconciliation explicitly. - [ ] Verify real native events in each advertised host, separately from synthetic hook tests. ## Alternatives considered Keep the current behavior and document its limits. This remains valid where the added guarantee has no user need; the issue should close with a documented product decision rather than assume that copying Hindsight is always appropriate. Reuse existing Cortex mechanisms before adding a second pipeline. ## Scope assessment HIGH. Raised from the October 10 Hindsight/Cortex comparison. Static observations refer to the pinned revisions below. They do not establish successful execution of Hindsight's whole pipeline or a repository-wide absence in Cortex. Priority is a proposal, not a release blocker. ## Evidence [mcp_server/infrastructure/transcript_rollout.py:44](https://github.com/cdeust/Cortex/blob/02c3cf006e7024811bcb379ce375e7eafd8267a9/mcp_server/infrastructure/transcript_rollout.py#L44); [mcp_server/hooks/session_lifecycle.py:351](https://github.com/cdeust/Cortex/blob/02c3cf006e7024811bcb379ce375e7eafd8267a9/mcp_server/hooks/session_lifecycle.py#L351); comparator [hindsight-integrations/coding-agents/src/core/retain-cursor.ts:44](https://github.com/vectorize-io/hindsight/blob/44d5340148fd47efb34e184d61f87ab5e2d8d1e2/hindsight-integrations/coding-agents/src/core/retain-cursor.ts#L44)

items.title: Kia US 260507 support (Sportage and others), and transaction codes looked up on the car
items.description: ### What would you like it to do? I'd like to use Light Studio on my Sportage Hybrid. Before I install it, there's one thing I'd like checked, and one small change that would make it safe to try on other cars. **The codes are fixed numbers from the Ioniq 6.** The engine sends raw binder transactions: - `ISystemService` 76/77/78 - `IUSMService` 0x130, 0x12f, 0x12e, 0x1bd–0x1c1 Each number is the method's position in that car's interface. On another build the same number can be a different method. My car's framework isn't the Ioniq 6's. From HMG-API's maps and my Car Report: | | `automotive.odex` | `framework.odex` | |---|---|---| | Ioniq 6 US 260507 (`hyundai/ceev/usa/260507`) | `173334b2…` | `81749415…` | | My Sportage Hybrid, `NQ5HEV.USA.0000.V015.012.260507` (`kia/nq5/usa/260507`) | `6a8b1492…` | `d592b4c9…` | The codes might still line up, but nothing checks that they do. On USM especially, a mismatched code could land on a different vehicle setting, because USM also handles things like seat heat. Light Studio doesn't check the build first, unlike your Split Screen Blocker's `RightScreenHome.odex` MD5 check. **Suggestion:** at startup, look the codes up on the car instead of hard-coding them. Read the `TRANSACTION_ ` constants from each interface's generated `Stub` class by reflection. For example: - `com.hkmc.micom.ISystemService$Stub.TRANSACTION_setSMLRGB` - `com.hkmc.usm.IUSMService$Stub.TRANSACTION_setDualLightALL` If one is missing, log it and leave the light alone. This would make Light Studio safe on any car, and correct on cars whose numbering differs. A smaller step would be an MD5 gate on `automotive.odex` (and wherever `IUSMService` lives), like Split Screen Blocker's. **Two-zone vs one-zone:** I'm not sure my Sportage has a separate lower light. If the car only has the upper zone, it would help if Light Studio detected that (or offered an "upper only" option) instead of sending `setDualLightALL`. The same framework build is listed in HMG-API's `kia/nq5/usa/260507` map for the Sportage (gas, Hybrid, Plug-in Hybrid), Forte, Carnival 2022, Niro Hybrid and Plug-in Hybrid, Soul, and Seltos 2024. One check would cover all of them. I'm happy to test a build on my car and send the log, including the codes it finds. [car-report-nq5hev-usa-260507-20261118-1623.json](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/35060044/car-report-nq5hev-usa-260507-20261118-1623.json) ### Your car 2023 Kia Sportage Hybrid, US

items.description: Part of #1 · Module **`accounting-adapter (Tally) — module decided with the decision below`** · Migrations **next free in the module's band, allocated in `DATA-MODEL.md` at build** · Screens **as named in Scope** · Severity **blocker** · Finding type **MISSING-TASK** · Related: #663, #174, #173, #175, #677, #801, neetub1508/accounting#78 · Source: Grok competitor gap analysis 2026-11-13, REQ-03 > **Needs decision.** #663 Q-D4 was decided by the R33 decision rule: 'TallyPrime XML in accounting (accounting#78), no warehouse setting'. That covers customers who run OrbitPi accounting. It leaves out the reference configuration D-7 (warehouse standalone) where the books stay in Tally, which is exactly the Fast WMS buyer. Decide: (a) warehouse-only installs get Tally through a thin adapter on the warehouse handover queue that reuses accounting#78's Tally XML builder, mapping and transport, or (b) Tally is offered only with OrbitPi accounting. Recommendation: (a). Nothing in accounting#78 is duplicated by this issue. ## Why this task exists In Indian SMB and mid-market deals the accountant already runs TallyPrime, and the first question is 'will it post to Tally?'. Fast WMS answers yes (GRN, dispatch and invoices posted as Tally vouchers) and also offers a two-way SAP/Oracle link. Our website has to say there is no direct Tally connector. accounting#78 adds Tally XML export and per-voucher posting for the OrbitPi accounting ledger; a customer who buys only OrbitPi Warehouse still re-keys every GRN and dispatch into Tally. The warehouse handover queue and envelopes (#173, #174) already carry every accountable warehouse event, so only the Tally sink for warehouse-only installs is missing. ## Scope - A Tally sink on the warehouse-base accounting handover queue, active only when OrbitPi accounting is not installed, reusing accounting#78's voucher XML builder, release pinning and per-voucher status model (no second Tally engine). - Master mapping with maker-checker: OrbitPi company/GSTIN -> Tally company; item -> stock item (name, alias or part number #801, units, HSN); site/zone/status store -> godown; counterparty -> party ledger (GSTIN first); handover kind -> voucher type and ledgers; cost centre -> Tally cost centre. items.title: [sdk] Add WalletConnect 2.0 deep link support for mobile wallet signing
items.description: ## ✨ Enhancement — SDK ## Problem The SDK supports WalletConnect but does not generate deep links for mobile wallets (e.g., Lobstr, LOBSTR Mobile). Users on mobile need deep links to switch to their wallet app for signing. ## Proposed solution - Detect mobile environment (`/Android|iOS/i.test(navigator.userAgent)`) - Generate a WalletConnect 2.0 deep link (`wc:...` URI) for mobile wallet apps - Open the deep link via `window.location.href` (native app routing) - After signing, the wallet returns the user to Linkora via universal link - Fallback: QR code for cross-device signing ## Acceptance criteria - [ ] Mobile environment detected automatically - [ ] WC 2.0 deep link generated for mobile wallets - [ ] Deep link opens Lobstr / compatible wallet on Android and iOS - [ ] Universal link returns user to Linkora after signing - [ ] QR code fallback for cross-device use - [ ] Tested on Android and iOS simulators

items.title: #111 harness: omp 18.11.1 마찰 ③ — CoW 워크트리 복제 시 .omp/harness-state 격리 + commitTargetDir 선행 cd 정합화
items.description: ## 맥락 `omp 18.4.3`의 `PI_SMART_GIT=1` / `worktree.clone`(Copy-on-Write 워크트리 복제)과 `18.8.6`의 `worktree.onStart`가 하네스의 워크트리 격리 계약(#58)과 충돌해요. 상세 분석: `docs/handoff/handoff_2026-10-16_omp-18-11-1-friction-audit.md` §3 F8·§4 F9. 사이클 ①/②와 독립이며 선택 사이클이에요. ## 마찰 지점 | ID | 심각도 | 내용 | 근거 | |---|---|---|---| | F9 | 높음 | CoW 복제는 `node_modules/`뿐 아니라 **모든 gitignored 파일**을 새 워크트리에 복제해요. `.omp/harness-state/`(`backpressure-status`, `read-log.txt`, `gated-commit-token` 등)와 `docs/reviews/`가 그대로 따라가서, **새 워크트리에서 파일을 읽지 않고 편집하거나 테스트 없이 커밋해도 게이트가 통과**해요 | `omp://tools/bash.md` Flow 5 `worktree.clone`; `.gitignore`의 `.omp/harness-state/`·`docs/reviews/` | | F8 | 낮음 | `git-commit-detect.mjs:886` `commitTargetDir()`는 `CWD_SHIFTERS`가 하나라도 있으면 `null`을 반환하지만, `cross-repo.mjs`의 `shellWriteTargets`와 #58 `verificationCwd`는 선행 리터럴 `cd &&` 1회를 추적해요. `cd && git commit …`에서 `cross-repo`는 통과하는데 `index.ts:239` `snapshotHead`가 스냅샷을 못 찍어 착지 판정이 reflog 대신 exit code 폴백으로 떨어져요 | 세 함수의 `cd` 처리 불일치 | ## 해결 방향 - `read-tracker`/`write-tracker`/`context-gate`, `backpressure-tracker`/`backpressure-gate`가 상태 파일에 워크트리 실경로(`realpathSync(cwd)`) 헤더·메타를 기록하고, 읽을 때 불일치하면 stale/untrusted로 무시해요(복제된 상태 파일 무효화). - 최소 대안: `harness-harness_integration_contract.md`와 `gh-loop`/`gh-fanout` 스킬에 `PI_SMART_GIT=1`/`worktree.clone` 사용 시 `.omp/harness-state/` 초기화 주의와, `worktree.onStart: true`가 모든 세션을 링크드 워크트리로 띄워 #68 `harness-check` 가드에 걸린다는 점을 안내해요. - F8은 `commitTargetDir`도 `verificationCwd`/`shellWriteTargets`와 같은 규칙(선행 `cd &&` 1회 허용)으로 정합화할지 결정해요. - 관련: #51(같은 워크트리 서브에이전트의 harness-state 오염 — 격리 설계가 겹치면 함께 다뤄요). ## AC - [ ] 다른 워크트리 경로에서 복제된 `.omp/harness-state/`(`backpressure-status=PASS`, `read-log.txt` 항목)가 새 워크트리에서 PASS/읽음 증거로 인정되지 않음이 단위 테스트로 증명돼요. - [ ] `commitTargetDir("cd && git commit -m x")`의 동작(추적 또는 `null` 유지)이 결정되고 테스트로 고정돼요. - [ ] `harness-harness_integration_contract.md`에 CoW 복제·`worktree.onStart` 주의가 기록돼요. - [ ] `node --test .omp/extensions/harness/tests/*.test.mjs` 전 항목 통과해요.

items.title: Ask HN: When does your app need its own UI vs. using it via MCP?
items.description: I'd love to hear HN user's views on when they think an app their building needs a UI vs just supplies data via MCP to Claude/ChatGPT. If Claude/ChatGPT is where the bulk of work is done in the future (perhaps analogous to a general purpose computer) then how should app developers build in this world?

items.title: Ask HN: Tips for transitioning from web development to embedded/firmware?
items.description: I started my career 15+ years ago doing native development (c, c++, etc), but the last decade I've been doing fullstack web applications. I'd like to transition closer to my roots with a job doing primarily c, c++ or rust. The natural place seems to be in embedded development or firmware work. How feasible is the transition this late in the game? Any advice?

items.title: Ask HN: If AI tools are so good, why isn't your bug backlog empty?
items.description: A lot of people outside tech ask me if AI is going to replace programmers and I just think: if that were the case we should be running out of things to do The bug backlog should be empty and we've caught up to every feature request from PMs to the point that we are bottlenecked on the business side But that does not seem to be the case with my own company or most devs I talk to in the industry So what gives?

items.title: Ask HN: How do you reach the flow with vibe coding?
items.description: When I used to code without AI (probably not even one year ago), I sometimes reached a state of "flow" and it truly was a great feeling. Nowadays, I rarely code from scratch and most of my development (at work, at least) comes through AI. I get it that I can still code "the old way" in my free time, but I'm more curious to understand if people in a similar situation can reach the same state by vibe/AI coding, and how.

items.title: Ask HN: How do you use AI to get more relevant content?
items.description: The "algorithm" tries to give your attention something to eat. Sometimes, it's exactly what you want/need. Sometimes it's just meh , and not particularly enriching. Are any folks using AI to aggregate and rank content across YouTube, HackerNews, Twitter/X, Instagram etc. that's learns from your preferences to find enriching content not just entertaining content?

items.title: Ask HN: What are you working on? (November 2026)
items.description: What are you working on? What have you been curious about lately?

items.title: Ask HN: What was your weirdest or funniest job rejection?
items.description: I will start with mine. After the "Product Interview", where we spent 80% of the time discussing a feature from the user’s perspective, I got this feedback: > While your extensive experience with Go, database migrations, and reliability engineering stood out, as well as your strong problem-solving skills in coding exercises, we felt there were gaps in areas critical to this role, such as AI fluency and a deeper focus on production-quality considerations like testing and logging. These areas were key factors in our decision not to move forward. Which I find very funny. What was yours?

items.title: Ask HN: Are the more software malfunctions now than before?
items.description: I have the feeling (reading HN every day for the past 15 years) that the amount of major software malfunctions has increased drastically over the last year, maybe two. I remember that back in 2016-17 big failure events (cloud outages, critical infrastructure issues etc) were special discussion topics. Today they feel more like a routine event. If you also believe it's the case, what could be the reason? Cultural shift towards software? Global load increase? AI slop?
